name: Equal-risk-contribution (true risk parity) across 9 asset-class ETFs, 126-day covariance, monthly
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 127. Need >= 5 eligible else {}. Let N = eligible count and S = N x N sample covariance of daily r(k) for k = e-125..e. Start w_i = 1/N. Repeat 200 times: v = S w; sp2 = w'v; RC_i = w_i v_i; w_i <- w_i * sqrt((sp2/N)/RC_i) (if RC_i <= 0 leave w_i unchanged); renormalise w to sum 1. Output the final w (fully invested, no leverage, no signal, no cash). This equalises each ETF's contribution to portfolio variance (Maillard-Roncalli-Teiletche); the registry only has inverse-vol sizing, never ERC with correlations.
rationale: Inverse-vol ignores correlation; ERC corrects for it and is the textbook risk-parity construction behind all-weather style funds. Tests whether correlation-aware risk budgeting beats the same-asset equal-weight benchmark after costs.
source: Maillard, Roncalli & Teiletche 2010, 'The properties of equally weighted risk contribution portfolios', Journal of Portfolio Management 36(4), 60-70

name: Long-only minimum-variance sectors with constant-correlation shrinkage, 252-day, monthly
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 6 eligible else {}. Let S = sample covariance of daily r(k), k = e-251..e, over the N eligible symbols; rbar = mean of the N(N-1)/2 sample correlations; target F: F_ii = S_ii, F_ij = rbar*sqrt(S_ii S_jj); Sigma = 0.5*S + 0.5*F. Active set A = all eligible. Loop: solve x = Sigma_A^{-1} 1 (Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting), w_A = x / sum(x); if any w_i < 0 remove the symbol with the most negative w_i from A and repeat; stop when all w_i >= 0. Output w on A, 0 elsewhere. Constant-correlation shrinkage follows Ledoit-Wolf 2003 with the intensity fixed a priori at 0.5 (not estimated).
rationale: Low-risk anomaly and Clarke-de Silva-Thorley show the min-variance portfolio earns equity-like returns at lower risk; shrinkage keeps the 11-asset covariance invertible and stable. Never tested on sector ETFs (the registry has only the stock-universe version).
source: Clarke, de Silva & Thorley 2006, 'Minimum-variance portfolios in the U.S. equity market', Journal of Portfolio Management 33(1); Ledoit & Wolf 2003, 'Honey, I shrunk the sample covariance matrix', Journal of Portfolio Management 30(4)

name: Minimum Correlation Algorithm weights across 12 cross-asset ETFs, 252-day, monthly
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 8 eligible else {}. Over k = e-251..e compute sd_i of r(k) and the correlation matrix rho. mu, s = mean and sample std of the N(N-1)/2 distinct off-diagonal rho_ij. A_ij = 1 - Phi((rho_ij - mu)/s) for i != j, A_ii = 0 (Phi = standard normal CDF via the Abramowitz-Stegun 7.1.26 erf approximation). a_i = mean over j != i of A_ij. p_i = rank of a_i ascending (smallest a = 1, largest = N, ties by symbol) divided by sum of ranks. q = A p (vector), q_i / sum(q). w_i proportional to q_i / sd_i, renormalised to sum 1. This is the Varadi-Kapler-Bajaj-Zhang MinCorr heuristic, which needs no matrix inversion.
rationale: A practitioner portfolio rule explicitly built to put weight on low-correlation diversifiers without optimiser instability; a widely used alternative to Markowitz and risk parity that has no test here.
source: Varadi, Kapler, Bajaj & Zhang 2012, 'Minimum Correlation Algorithm: enhancing diversification through correlation', CSS Analytics white paper (cssanalytics.wordpress.com)

name: Three-factor residual momentum across 22 ETFs (factors QQQ, IEF, DBC), months 12-2 residual, monthly
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Factor ETFs: QQQ, IEF, DBC (excluded as candidates; they only supply factor returns). Candidates = the other 22 ETFs. Eligible: L > 253 for the candidate and all three factors. For candidate s over k = e-251..e do OLS of r_s(k) on [1, r_QQQ(k), r_IEF(k), r_DBC(k)] to get betas b (3) and intercept; residual u(k) = r_s(k) - b . f(k) (intercept NOT removed, so the residual keeps the asset's own drift). score_s = sum of u(k) for k = e-251..e-21 divided by the sample std of u(k) over k = e-251..e-21. Hold the 5 highest scores equally (1/5). Need >= 10 eligible else {}. Skip-month is applied (last 21 days excluded from the score). Candidates exclude the three factor ETFs QQQ, IEF and DBC (a factor regressed on itself has a zero residual and a 0/0 score); they stay in meta.assets as regressors only. 'Need >= 10 eligible' counts candidates (the other 22 ETFs).
rationale: Residual momentum strips out the exposure to common equity, duration and commodity factors, so it ranks idiosyncratic persistence rather than which factor happened to rally; Blitz-Huij-Martens find it has about twice the Sharpe of raw momentum. The registry only has market-residual sector momentum (acad-55); this is a cross-asset three-factor version.
source: Blitz, Huij & Martens 2011, 'Residual momentum', Journal of Empirical Finance 18(3), 506-521

name: Intermediate momentum: top 6 of 25 ETFs by the return from 12 to 7 months ago (skips the latest 7 months), monthly
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 12 eligible else {}. score_s = c(e-147)/c(e-252) - 1. Hold the 6 highest scores equally (1/6); no absolute filter. Distinct from 12-1 momentum, which includes months 6-2.
rationale: Novy-Marx shows momentum is driven by the return 12 to 7 months back and that recent 6-month winners add little; if that holds across asset classes it gives a skip-month variant with lower turnover than 12-1. Not in the registry for ETFs (crypto weekly analogue only).
source: Novy-Marx 2012, 'Is momentum really momentum?', Journal of Financial Economics 103(3), 429-453

name: Dispersion-gated sector momentum: momentum only in low-dispersion months, equal-weight otherwise (Stivers-Sun)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 275; need >= 8 eligible else {}. For any index k define disp(k) = sample std across the eligible sectors of the 21-day return c(k)/c(k-21) - 1. D = disp(e); med = median of disp(e-21j) for j = 1..12. mom_s = c(e-21)/c(e-252) - 1. If D < med: hold the 3 highest mom_s equally (1/3). Else: hold all eligible sectors equally (1/N). median of the 12 values = mean of the 6th and 7th smallest.
rationale: Stivers-Sun find the momentum premium is weak after high cross-sectional dispersion and value strong; the rule asks if sector momentum is worth holding only when dispersion is low, versus the EW sector benchmark otherwise. The registry has dispersion only as an equity timing gate and a stock-universe switch.
source: Stivers & Sun 2010, 'Cross-sectional return dispersion and time variation in value and momentum premiums', Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 45(4), 987-1014

name: Average-correlation regime switch on sectors: momentum when correlation is low, low-volatility when it is high
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 316; need >= 8 eligible else {}. avgcorr(k) = mean of all pairwise Pearson correlations of the eligible sectors' daily r over the 63 bars ending at k. AC = avgcorr(e); med = median of avgcorr(e-21j) for j = 1..12. If AC <= med (dispersed, stock-picking regime): hold the 3 highest mom_s = c(e-21)/c(e-252)-1 equally. If AC > med (crowded regime): hold the 3 lowest sd of r over the last 126 days equally. median of the 12 values = mean of the 6th and 7th smallest.
rationale: High average correlation marks macro-driven markets where relative momentum is unreliable and defensive low-vol sectors protect; low correlation marks sector-specific markets where momentum works. A cross-sectional rotation, unlike the registry's average-correlation market timing.
source: Pollet & Wilson 2010, 'Average correlation and stock market returns', Journal of Financial Economics 96(3), 364-380; Kritzman, Li, Page & Rigobon 2011, 'Principal components as a measure of systemic risk', Journal of Portfolio Management 37(4)

name: Absorption-ratio shift gate on sector momentum (Kritzman et al.), defensive IEF when the shift z > 1
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Candidates: the 11 sectors; IEF is the defensive asset only (never ranked). Eligible: L > 481 for sectors (need >= 8) and IEF. For index k, let C(k) = correlation matrix of the eligible sectors' daily r over the 250 bars ending at k, n = its size. AR(k) = (lambda1 + lambda2)/n, where lambda1, lambda2 = the top two eigenvalues of C(k) by power iteration (100 iterations; start vector for the first = (1,..,1)/sqrt(n); deflate C - lambda1 v1 v1' and start the second from (1,-1,1,-1,..)/sqrt(n)). Use k = e-21j for j = 0..11. z = (AR(e) - mean_j AR) / sample std_j AR. If z > 1: hold IEF 100%. Else hold the 3 highest 12-1 sector returns c(e-21)/c(e-252)-1 equally.
rationale: A high or rising absorption ratio means sector returns are driven by one factor and markets are fragile; Kritzman et al. show spikes precede drawdowns. Never tested here as a regime gate on a rotation.
source: Kritzman, Li, Page & Rigobon 2011, 'Principal components as a measure of systemic risk', Journal of Portfolio Management 37(4), 112-126

name: Sharpe-ranked ETF rotation: top 6 of 25 by 126-day return/volatility, inverse-volatility weights, positive scores only
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 127; need >= 10 eligible else {}. m_s = mean of r(k), sd_s = sample std of r(k), k = e-125..e; score_s = m_s/sd_s. Candidates = score_s > 0. Take up to the 6 highest; if fewer than 3 candidates return {}. w_s proportional to 1/sd_s, normalised to sum 1 over the picks. Cross-sectional ranking by risk-adjusted return, not raw return.
rationale: Raw-return ranking over-selects the most volatile ETFs (UNG, SLV, USO); ranking by return per unit risk puts bonds and defensives in contention and sizes by risk. A widely used 'risk-adjusted momentum' filter that the registry has only on time-series sizing.
source: Barroso & Santa-Clara 2015, 'Momentum has its moments', Journal of Financial Economics 116(1), 111-120; Dudler, Gmuer & Malamud 2014, 'Risk-adjusted time series momentum'

name: Frog-in-the-pan continuous momentum on ETFs: among the top 10 by 12-1, hold the 5 with the smoothest path
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 12 eligible else {}. PRET_s = c(e-21)/c(e-252) - 1. Over the formation days k = e-251..e-21 (231 daily returns) let pos = share with r(k) > 0 and neg = share with r(k) < 0. ID_s = sign(PRET_s) * (neg - pos) (more negative = more continuous). Candidates = the 10 highest PRET_s with PRET_s > 0. Hold the 5 candidates with the lowest ID equally (1/5, or 1/n if fewer than 5 but >= 3; else {}).
rationale: Da-Gurun-Warachka find momentum built from many small gains persists while momentum from a few large jumps reverses; ETFs are the cleanest test of whether the smoothness filter generalises beyond stocks.
source: Da, Gurun & Warachka 2014, 'Frog in the pan: continuous information and momentum', Review of Financial Studies 27(7), 2171-2218

name: Downside-beta premium on sectors: hold the 4 of 11 with the highest beta in down-market days, monthly
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 8 eligible else {}. M(k) = mean of the eligible sectors' r(k) (equal-weight sector market). Over k = e-251..e let mu = mean of M; D = {k : M(k) < mu}. beta_down_s = cov(r_s, M over D) / var(M over D). Hold the 4 highest beta_down_s equally (1/4).
rationale: Ang-Chen-Xing show assets that fall hardest with the market in down states earn a risk premium beyond ordinary beta; the registry tests downside beta on stocks and crypto but never on a sector-ETF cross-section.
source: Ang, Chen & Xing 2006, 'Downside risk', Review of Financial Studies 19(4), 1191-1239

name: Asset-class-neutral momentum: best 2 equity ETFs, best bond, best commodity by 12-1, inverse-volatility weighted
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Classes (fixed): EQ = QQQ DIA XLK XLF XLE XLV XLI XLP XLY XLU XLB XLC VNQ; BOND = TLT IEF SHY LQD HYG AGG; COMM = GLD SLV USO UNG DBC. UUP is never held. Eligible: L > 253. mom_s = c(e-21)/c(e-252) - 1. Picks: the 2 highest mom in EQ, the 1 highest in BOND, the 1 highest in COMM (need all 4 else {}). sd_s = sample std of r over the last 126 bars. w_s proportional to 1/sd_s, normalised to sum 1. No absolute filter (pure relative momentum inside each class).
rationale: Top-N across all 25 ETFs concentrates in whichever class is trending; forcing one winner per class is the Asness-Moskowitz-Pedersen 'everywhere' design and a common retail ETF-rotation shape. Registry has pooled top-N only.
source: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen 2013, 'Value and momentum everywhere', Journal of Finance 68(3), 929-985

name: Overnight-return momentum across 13 equity ETFs: top 4 by 12-1 sum of overnight (close-to-open) log returns
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 254; need >= 8 eligible else {}. overnight(k) = ln(b[k].open / c(k-1)). score_s = sum of overnight(k) for k = e-251..e-21. Hold the 4 highest scores equally (1/4). Uses only bars up to e (open of bar k is known at the open of k, before the close at e). Disclosure: the cached bars are unadjusted, so ex-dividend gaps sit inside overnight(k); accepted as-is (same data every other test uses) and not corrected.
rationale: Lou-Polk-Skouras find momentum profits accrue overnight while intraday returns reverse, so ranking on the overnight component isolates the persistent part. The registry's overnight test is a single-index time-series rule; this is the cross-sectional version on sector ETFs.
source: Lou, Polk & Skouras 2019, 'A tug of war: overnight versus intraday expected returns', Journal of Financial Economics 134(1), 192-213

name: High-volume return premium on 13 equity ETFs: hold the 4 with the highest 5-day volume vs their 1-year average
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 8 eligible else {}. vr_s = mean(volume, k = e-4..e) / mean(volume, k = e-251..e) (b[k].volume, shares). Hold the 4 highest vr_s equally (1/4), regardless of price direction.
rationale: Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin find unusually high trading volume raises the next month's return through increased visibility, whatever the sign of the volume-day return. ETF volume is partly arbitrage flow, so this is a genuine test of whether the visibility premium survives in ETFs.
source: Gervais, Kaniel & Mingelgrin 2001, 'The high-volume return premium', Journal of Finance 56(3), 877-919

name: Trend t-statistic ranking: top 6 of 25 ETFs by the t-stat of the 126-day log-price slope, monthly
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 127; need >= 10 eligible else {}. For k = e-125..e, x = 0..125, y = ln c(k); OLS slope beta and its standard error SE = sqrt((SSE/124)/Sxx); t_s = beta/SE. Candidates: t_s > 0. Hold up to the 6 highest t_s equally; fewer than 3 candidates returns {}. The t-statistic rewards slope per unit of residual noise, so smooth trends rank above jumpy ones.
rationale: Baltas-Kosowski show regression t-stat trend signals have lower turnover and better risk-adjusted performance than raw lookback returns in futures; this transfers the statistic to a cross-sectional ETF rotation.
source: Baltas & Kosowski 2013, 'Momentum strategies in futures markets and trend-following funds', SSRN 1968996

name: Correlation-capped diversified momentum: walk down the 12-1 ranking, skip any ETF with 126-day correlation > 0.7 to a holding
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 12 eligible else {}. mom_s = c(e-21)/c(e-252) - 1; sort descending (ties by symbol). selected = []. For each symbol in order with mom_s > 0: compute Pearson correlation of daily r over k = e-125..e with every selected symbol; select it only if all correlations <= 0.7; stop at 5 selected. If fewer than 3 selected return {}. Equal weight over those selected.
rationale: Plain top-5 momentum often holds four near-identical sector ETFs; the correlation cap forces breadth across equity, bond and commodity trends. Practitioners do this by hand; there is no test of whether it improves on the plain top-N.
source: Varadi (CSS Analytics) 'correlation-adjusted momentum selection' practitioner method; Keller & van Putten 2012, 'Generalized momentum and flexible asset allocation (FAA)', SSRN 2193735

name: Tranched weekly momentum: average of the last four weekly top-5 12-1 portfolios (rebalance-timing-luck fix)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance weekly. Eligible per tranche date: L > 253. For j = 0,1,2,3 let t_j = e - 5j. Tranche portfolio P_j: using only bars up to t_j, mom_s = c(t_j-21)/c(t_j-252) - 1 (c evaluated at those indices), hold the 5 highest equally (1/5 each; need >= 10 eligible else P_j empty). Final weights = (P_0 + P_1 + P_2 + P_3)/4 per symbol (sum <= 1).
rationale: A single monthly rebalance date makes results depend on a calendar accident ('timing luck'); averaging four staggered portfolios holds the same signal with smoother turnover. The common 12-1 top-5 is tested only with one rebalance date.
source: Hoffstein, Faber & Braun 2020, 'Rebalance timing luck: the (dumb) luck of the rebalance date', Newfound Research / SSRN 3673910

name: 12-1 momentum with a 10% per-holding stop-loss and cash-to-SHY, monthly entry, daily checks (Han-Zhou-Zhu) on 25 ETFs
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY', rank() mode, rebalance daily (needed to check the stop; only stops and month starts change weights). Anchor a = the index of the first bar in the view whose UTC calendar month equals the month of b[e]. Eligible at a: L > 253 (use universe views truncated at a: mom_s = c(a-21)/c(a-252) - 1, 5 highest, need >= 10 eligible else {}). For each pick p (initial weight 0.2): if c(k) <= 0.90*c(a) for ANY k = a+1..e then p is stopped (stays out until the next month's anchor) and its 0.2 is given to SHY instead. Output pick weights + SHY residual (SHY may also be a pick; weights add). On e = a nothing is stopped. Stop is on closing prices. 'First bar in the view' and the index arithmetic are applied per symbol by calendar date (all symbols share the same trading calendar), so a, e and k refer to the same dates for every symbol.
rationale: Han-Zhou-Zhu show a simple 10% stop-loss cuts momentum crash risk dramatically in stocks; ETF momentum has smaller left tails, so this asks whether the stop pays for its whipsaw cost. Registry has stop-loss momentum only for US stocks.
source: Han, Zhou & Zhu 2016, 'Taming momentum crashes: a simple stop-loss strategy', SSRN 2407199

name: Volatility-contraction momentum: among sectors with positive 126-day return, hold the 4 with the lowest 21d/126d volatility ratio
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance weekly. Eligible: L > 127; need >= 8 eligible else {}. Candidates: c(e)/c(e-126) - 1 > 0. vc_s = sd(r over last 21 bars) / sd(r over last 126 bars). Hold the 4 candidates with the lowest vc_s equally; fewer than 2 candidates returns {}.
rationale: A trend whose recent volatility has contracted below its own norm is the 'tight base' continuation setup traders use (VCP); here it is a rule-based cross-sectional filter to test if quiet leaders outperform loud ones.
source: Minervini 2013, 'Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard' (McGraw-Hill), volatility-contraction pattern; Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen 2012 for the underlying trend premium

name: Momentum plus low-volatility rank combination: 6 of 25 ETFs with the best sum of 12-1 rank and 252d low-volatility rank
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 12 eligible else {}. rankM_s = rank of mom_s = c(e-21)/c(e-252)-1 (1 = highest). rankV_s = rank of sd(r over last 252 bars) (1 = lowest). composite = rankM + rankV. Hold the 6 lowest composites equally (ties: lower rankM, then symbol).
rationale: Momentum and low volatility are the two anomalies with the most robust evidence and they are negatively correlated, so a rank blend selects trending assets that are not wild. The registry combines momentum with value (acad-08) but never with low volatility.
source: Blitz & van Vliet 2018, 'The Conservative Formula: quantitative investing made easy', Journal of Portfolio Management 44(7), 24-38; Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen 2019, 'Quality minus junk'

name: Relative-price dip in an uptrend: buy the 3 sectors most oversold versus the sector average (60-day z-score) that are above their 200-day SMA, weekly
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance weekly. Eligible: L > 260; need >= 8 eligible else {}. For k = e-59..e: RP_s(k) = ln(c_s(k)/c_s(e-59)) - (mean over eligible s' of ln(c_s'(k)/c_s'(e-59))). z_s = (RP_s(e) - mean_k RP_s(k)) / sample std_k RP_s(k) over those 60 values. Candidates: c_s(e) > mean of c_s over the last 200 bars. Hold the 3 candidates with the lowest z_s equally; fewer than 3 candidates returns {}.
rationale: Dip-buying in leaders is the commonest retail rule; the relative-price z-score measures the dip against peers (not against the sector's own price), and the 200-day filter keeps it out of broken trends. Tests relative reversion inside uptrends rather than the registry's raw 1-week or 1-month sector reversals.
source: Lo, Mamaysky & Wang 2000, 'Foundations of technical analysis', Journal of Finance 55(4); Connors & Alvarez 2009, 'Short Term Trading Strategies That Work' (buy pullbacks in uptrends)

name: Unanimous multi-horizon momentum: 5 of 25 ETFs with the best worst-rank across 1, 3, 6 and 12 month returns
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 12 eligible else {}. For n in {21, 63, 126, 252}: ret_n = c(e)/c(e-n) - 1; rank_n = rank among eligible (1 = highest). worst_s = max over n of rank_n. Hold the 5 lowest worst_s equally (ties: lower sum of the four ranks, then symbol).
rationale: Requiring strength on every horizon at once (a minimax, not an average) avoids assets whose 12-month return hides a recent break. The registry averages ranks (redteam-36) and gates on trend; this is the only intersection rule.
source: Keller & van Putten 2012, 'Generalized momentum and flexible asset allocation (FAA)', SSRN 2193735; Jegadeesh & Titman 1993

name: Up/down capture ratio sectors: hold the 4 of 11 with the best 252-day up-capture over down-capture versus the sector average
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 8 eligible else {}. M(k) = mean of the eligible sectors' r(k). Over k = e-251..e: up_s = mean(r_s(k) | M(k) > 0) / mean(M(k) | M(k) > 0); dn_s = mean(r_s(k) | M(k) < 0) / mean(M(k) | M(k) < 0). ratio_s = up_s / max(dn_s, 0.05). Hold the 4 highest ratios equally.
rationale: Capture ratios are the standard fund-selection statistic (Morningstar) for who rises with the market but falls less; as a sector rule it is an asymmetry screen different from beta or momentum.
source: Morningstar capture-ratio methodology (Morningstar Research, 'Morningstar Risk Statistics'); Ang, Chen & Xing 2006 for the asymmetric-beta motivation

name: Skip-week quarterly momentum, weekly rebalance: top 4 of 13 equity ETFs by the 13-week return ending one week ago
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance weekly. Eligible: L > 70; need >= 8 eligible else {}. score_s = c(e-5)/c(e-65) - 1 (13 weeks back, last 5 trading days skipped to avoid the short-term reversal). Hold the 4 highest equally (1/4).
rationale: Gutierrez-Kelley document that weekly returns continue for up to a year after the one-week reversal; a skip-week 13-week formation on weekly rebalancing is a faster, shorter-horizon cousin of 12-1 that the registry's monthly rules never test.
source: Gutierrez & Kelley 2008, 'The long-lasting momentum in weekly returns', Journal of Finance 63(1), 415-447; Lehmann 1990, 'Fads, martingales, and market efficiency', QJE 105(1)

name: Dollar-neutral sector momentum: long the top 3, short the bottom 3 of 11 sectors by 12-1, monthly (Moskowitz-Grinblatt)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). longShort true. Eligible: L > 253; need >= 8 eligible else {}. mom_s = c(e-21)/c(e-252) - 1. Long the 3 highest at +1/6 each; short the 3 lowest at -1/6 each (sum |w| = 1, net 0). Shorts pay no borrow in the harness (disclosed).
rationale: The original industry-momentum result is long-short; every registry sector momentum rule is long-only, so its raw cross-sectional spread has never been measured against the benchmark here.
source: Moskowitz & Grinblatt 1999, 'Do industries explain momentum?', Journal of Finance 54(4), 1249-1290

name: Calmar-ranked ETFs: top 6 of 25 by 252-day return divided by 252-day maximum drawdown, monthly
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 12 eligible else {}. ret = c(e)/c(e-252) - 1. maxdd = max over k in e-251..e of (peak(e-251..k) - c(k))/peak(e-251..k). calmar_s = ret / max(maxdd, 0.02). Candidates: calmar_s > 0. Hold up to the 6 highest equally; fewer than 3 returns {}.
rationale: Ranking by return per unit of drawdown (the CTA performance-review statistic) penalises assets that earned their return through a deep hole, which raw 12-month and even Sharpe ranking underweight.
source: Young 1991, 'Calmar ratio: a smoother tool', Futures Magazine; Eling & Schuhmacher 2007 on drawdown-based performance measures

name: Chaikin money-flow accumulation rank: 4 of 13 equity ETFs with the highest 63-day CMF above their 100-day SMA, monthly
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 101; need >= 8 eligible else {}. For k = e-62..e: mfm(k) = ((close-low) - (high-close)) / (high-low) with high==low giving 0; mfv(k) = mfm(k) * volume(k). CMF_s = sum mfv / sum volume over the 63 bars. Candidates: c(e) > mean of c over the last 100 bars. Hold the 4 candidates with the highest CMF equally; fewer than 2 candidates returns {}.
rationale: Volume-weighted close location is the classic accumulation/distribution gauge; ranking it cross-sectionally, with a trend filter, tests whether sustained closes near the highs on volume (a flow proxy) predicts the next month.
source: Chaikin, 'Chaikin Money Flow' (StockCharts ChartSchool); Wyckoff accumulation/distribution; Granville 1963, 'Granville's New Key to Stock Market Profits'

name: Variance-ratio trending filter on momentum: 12-1 leaders among the ETFs whose 5-day variance ratio exceeds 1 (trending), monthly
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 258; need >= 12 eligible else {}. d(k) = ln(c(k)/c(k-1)), k = e-251..e. q5(k) = d(k)+d(k-1)+d(k-2)+d(k-3)+d(k-4) for k = e-247..e. VR_s = sample var(q5) / (5 * sample var(d)). Candidates: VR_s > 1 AND c(e-21)/c(e-252) - 1 > 0. Hold up to 5 candidates with the highest 12-1 return equally; fewer than 2 candidates returns {}.
rationale: Momentum should work where returns are positively autocorrelated; the Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio measures this directly, so this tests if an ETF's own trending character separates working from non-working momentum.
source: Lo & MacKinlay 1988, 'Stock market prices do not follow random walks', Review of Financial Studies 1(1), 41-66

name: Low-volume momentum winners (Lee-Swaminathan): among the top 7 of 13 equity ETFs by 12-1, hold the 4 with the lowest recent volume
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). Eligible: L > 253; need >= 8 eligible else {}. mom_s = c(e-21)/c(e-252) - 1. Take the 7 highest. For each: v_s = mean(volume, k = e-62..e) / mean(volume, k = e-251..e). Hold the 4 of the 7 with the lowest v_s equally (1/4).
rationale: Lee-Swaminathan find high-volume winners are the late-stage ones that fade, while low-volume winners keep going; ETF volume partly reflects crowding, so the rule tests the volume 'life-cycle' of momentum on sector ETFs (the registry tests it only on US stocks).
source: Lee & Swaminathan 2000, 'Price momentum and trading volume', Journal of Finance 55(5), 2017-2069

name: Beta-hedged sector momentum: long the top 3 sectors by 12-1, short QQQ for their beta, monthly (relative strength only)
rule: Conventions: rank() mode; for symbol s, b = universe[s], e = b.length-1 (the rebalance-day close, the latest bar in the view); c(k) = b[k].close; r(k) = c(k)/c(k-1)-1; windows are counted back from e; a symbol absent from the view or with too little history for every window used is ineligible; sd = sample std (n-1); ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 (unless longShort) and sum of |weights| <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0; if fewer eligible picks than the stated minimum, return {} (cash that period). meta: universe 'ETFS_DAILY' restricted by meta.assets, rank() mode, rebalance monthly (harness fires on the last trading day of each month). longShort true. Candidates: the 11 sectors (QQQ is only the hedge). Eligible: L > 253 (QQQ and >= 8 sectors, else {}). mom_s = c(e-21)/c(e-252) - 1; long the 3 highest at +0.14 each. beta_s = cov(r_s, r_QQQ)/var(r_QQQ) over k = e-251..e. Short QQQ at weight -min(0.58, 0.14 * sum of the 3 betas). Total |w| <= 1. No borrow cost modelled (disclosed). The short-QQQ weight is floored at 0 (if the sum of the 3 betas is <= 0, no QQQ position is taken; never a long QQQ).
rationale: Long-only sector momentum is mostly market beta; hedging the beta with QQQ isolates whether the winners beat the market, which is the actual claim of relative-strength rotation.
source: Moskowitz & Grinblatt 1999, 'Do industries explain momentum?', Journal of Finance 54(4); Grundy & Martin 2001 on beta-neutralised momentum
